subject: DESIGN PASS (designer): work-item layer (#503 lead proposal) — confirm/challenge the surface + the work-item VIEW (#538) + persona-review record; confirm the flagged seams before adoption
body:
DESIGN PASS — the work-item layer (ASK C / #503, lead's proposal). You (designer) + advocate confirm the seams BEFORE adoption; the proposed items are NOT implemented yet. ONE concern (your position).

LEAD'S PROPOSAL (summary; ask lead for the full text if needed): WORKITEM = a store record {id, title, assignees[], featureBranchName, worktreeRef, status, reviews[]}; one WorkItem : N QueueItems via ONE additive nullable `workItemId?` on the queue item (standalone items behave exactly as today). SEAM/INVARIANTS: WorkItem is a STORE RECORD, not a git ref (branch is a git artifact); all reads/writes through the ONE `serve` broker (single writer). Four shape elements: (1) feature branch per work item — created/advanced UNDER OPERATOR AUTHORITY, not seats (#146: seats cannot commit/merge); (2) assigned seats VIEW read-only, STORE-MEDIATED (do not restore read tools to coordinators — F9/#144); (3) decouple queue<->work via `workItemId?`; (4) persona branch review = a RECORD {persona, reviewerSeat, verdict, notes} that INFORMS the operator's integration — NOT a seat-held merge gate; reviewer != author. Guardrails: store authoritative (not git); no seat git-write; no restored coordinator read tools; no implementation bundled.

YOUR JOB (design view): confirm or challenge the SURFACE — the work-item VIEW (#538, the first-extension candidate), the persona-review record's user-visible shape, and whether the store-mediated view is legible. Name any rejection with its reason.

SEAMS lead FLAGGED it could NOT read (#473 worktree lifecycle, D48/D49, D50 item-scoped commits, the Router queue tools) — the pass must CONFIRM these before adoption. Map to the design-first flow: lead + designer/advocate proposal pass BEFORE implementation. BACKLOG; never push/publish.
resultSummary:
DESIGN PASS (designer) — work-item layer (#503 lead proposal). One concern: the SURFACE.

## CONFIRMATIONS

**1. Store-record WorkItem + ONE nullable `workItemId?` — CONFIRM.** Grounded: D53's three-layer concurrency model (files concurrent / slots capped / store single-writer) already implies the work-item layer must be a STORE record, not a git ownership transfer. Precedent: `durig.seats`/`durig.edges`/`durig.constitution`/`durig.queue` are all session-scoped defineDoc records with plain values. The `workItemId?` additive nullable link preserves standalone-item behavior exactly (no backfill needed; old stores keep working).

**2. WorkItem as STORE record, not a git ref — CONFIRM with the load-bearing surface condition.** The store must be authoritative. Described in REJECTIONS below.

**3. Single-writer via the ONE `serve` broker — CONFIRM.** D45/D52/D53: "one broker (`serve`) owns the store and drives up to N seats, each in its own worktree"; "two drivers on one DB = NO". The WorkItem doc rides the existing harness; no new writer, no new socket, no new trust surface.

**4. Feature branch per work item — CREATED UNDER OPERATOR AUTHORITY, COMMITS BY THE DEVELOPER (D50), MERGE NEVER SEATS.** The proposal's "operator authority" language needs one sentence of reconciliation with D50 (which moved commit authority to the developer): the OPERATOR creates/advances the branch; the DEVELOPER commits item work to it; NOBODY EXCEPT THE OPERATOR merges. This is my design vantage; lead should state it in one sentence so a user does not have to read three decision entries to predict it.

**5. Assigned seats VIEW READ-ONLY, STORE-MEDIATED — CONFIRM.** No restored read tools for coordinators (F9/#144/D55: "a path a coordinator cannot open is worse than a body"). The work-item view reaches a seat through the EXISTING channels: claim_work/peek_queue results (thin-context inline or path) — NOT through new tools.

**6. Persona-review record {persona, reviewerSeat, verdict, notes} — CONFIRM the shape, with added fields.** Lead's "informs the operator's integration — NOT a seat-held merge gate" is CONFIRMED with the design reason: merge/integration is exactly the authority level durig has never given seats (push operator-only per constitution P2; commit moved to the developer by D50 with operator authorization; merge/integration is the operator's act, not a seat one). A seat-held merge gate also fails the distro test: a user must not need to know which seats merge.

## SURFACE — how a user sees this (legibility conditions)

**A. The WorkItem VIEW (status/watch/metrics) renders from readRigHealth ONLY.** Every WorkItem field must be readable when the worktree directory is GONE (worktree removal is successful+normal, D60, D48/D49) — "assignees pm/impl · branch wt/item-3 · worktree released · status integrated" comes from the STORE.

**B. Work-item rows follow the existing one-glyph vocabulary** (seatActivity precedent, watchview.mjs): one status glyph + status word per work item row. Status collapse shows 1 line + drill-down at 60 cols. Clutter audit: ONE glyph + status word; NO inline review list (that's a drill-down); NO inline branch-head.

**C. Review records must carry EVIDENCE** (command + exit code), not just the verdict. P1 Evidence ("a claim about durig is checked by RUNNING the demo suite; name the check and its exit code") applies to reviews as much as to completions. This is the same lesson D56 records for completions; same fix.

**D. The N:1 worktree question — a NEW shape consequence the proposal must answer.** Lead's shape is ONE `worktreeRef` per WorkItem, but the CURRENT implementation gives ONE worktree per QUEUE item (D49: "worktree-per-task lifecycle (create-on-claim, remove-on-complete/cancel)"). With one WorkItem : N QueueItems, either (a) one work item owns ONE worktree shared by its queue items (meaning the queue items' per-task lifecycle is re-pointed at the work item), or (b) N worktrees for one work item (meaning `worktreeRef` needs to be per queue item). I READ the proposal as (a) — the work item CLAIMS the worktree and holds the worktreeRef while its queue items ride along — and I propose recording that answer IN the shape.

**E. Failure legibility: the Dangling-ref condition must surface in attention.** `worktreeRef` can point at a removed directory while queue items are still non-terminal. It must surface as an attention notice (same channel as `idle_with_queued_work`), not as a silent gap.

## REJECTIONS (each with its reason)

**R1. REJECT: persona-review record as a MERGE GATE.** Reason: (i) merge/integration is the operator-only boundary durig's constitution explicitly draws (P2); (ii) D50 moved COMMIT (not merge) to the developer under operator authorization, and a seat-held merge gate re-litigates that boundary; (iii) the distro test — a normal user must not need to know which seats merge; (iv) the review's value is EVIDENCE the operator reads, not a gate that binds.

**R2. REJECT: any WORKITEM field derived from git state (branch heads, branch-existence, shas).** Reason: branch heads move (D50 authorizes developer commits; lead rules merge); a store record embedding a git-derived head goes stale silently — the exact "looks broken" failure D18/D11's decible fixed for databases. Store must be authoritative.

**R3. REJECT: restored read tools for work-item viewing (for coordinators or anyone).** Reason: F9/#144/D55 closed the coordinator-read gap with capability-keyed inline fallback; restoring tools re-opens it.

**R4. REJECT: a new wake/execution path for work items.** Reason: D45/D52/D53 — the ONE `serve` broker is the single writer; a second wake path re-runs the double-wake hazard D45/D46 exist to prevent. Work items are a VIEW over existing queue items, not a parallel execution path.

## THE SEAMS LEAD COULD NOT READ (#473 / D48 / D49 / D50 / Router queue tools) — CONFIRMED from code, by me:

- **#473 worktree lifecycle — CONFIRMED.** src/worktree.mjs: `claimWorktree` (create-on-claim → identity validation → lock → `npm ci --prefer-offline` → `rerere`), `removeClaimedWorktree` (unlock → junction/symlink refuse → `git worktree remove` → `.git` unlink → rm fallback), `listWorktrees`. This is the lifecycle the work-item layer must RIDE, not re-invent.
- **D48/D49 — CONFIRMED.** Per-task worktrees are the load-bearing isolation; the Job-Object helper reaps Windows process trees; `git worktree remove` (never `rm -rf`) with junction detection. Cleanup MANUAL (D60).
- **D50 item-scoped commits — CONFIRMED.** "whichever seat accepts the item commits that item's work", explicit-path staging only, push operator-only. A WorkItem must name WHO commits its branch, and the plan must not re-introduce an operator-commit step.
- **Router queue tools — CONFIRMED.** `enqueueItem` (transitions appends, `notice` flag, thin-context inline-body/path contract), `isDoneNotice` (structural now, subject-shaped legacy fallback — `workItemId` must NOT be derived from subject shape), `isTerminalItem`, `thinResultText` (D55), `RigQueue` defineDoc.

## OPEN SURFACE QUESTION (design-side) for lead/pm to answer before adoption

Where should `workItems` appear FIRST? My read is `(status and watch)` — additive fields in the existing JSON that the TUI/status/watch contracts already render — rather than a new verb. The METRICS.md admissibility rule ("actionable, rare when abnormal, and not already visible") suggests the TUI card is the FIRST surface; the CLI/status row is the SECOND; a dedicated `workitem` verb is NOT needed now (it would add surface area without removing some).
